Applications that use USDKit for accessing USD data will automatically have edits to the USD data synced with Spatial Preview Sessions.
When your app has its own USD runtime, the two applications don’t share memory or a stage cache.
For each direction, app to device and device to app, the pattern is the same: write overrides into a thin edit layer, export it to disk, and use to propagate the changes into USDKit’s stage.
When you read edits from the Spatial Preview stage and apply them to the in your application, don’t treat the edits as new changes to the USD data.
Batch and pass edits from an external OpenUSD runtime to the bridge layer at some reasonable time period (30ms for example) to prevent locking the thread.
